name: General Topology

papers.title: Characterizing $T_0$-spaces where GIS-convergence is topological
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate the GIS-convergence in $T_0$-spaces and the related concept of GIS-continuous spaces(GSI-continuous spaces). It is proved that $SI(X)$ is a locally hypercompact space iff $(X, \tau)$ is a $GSI$-continuous space iff GSI-convergence in $X$ with respect to the topology $\mathcal{O}_{SI}(X)$ is topological. We also show that the $GIS$-convergence in $(X, \tau)$ is topological if and only if $(X,\tau)$ is a $GIS$-continuous space.

papers.title: Smyth completeness and nonexpansive iteration in $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric spaces
papers.abstract: We study the specialization order $\le_d$, defined by $x\le_d y$ if and only if $d(x,y)=0$, of a $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric space $(X,d)$. We show that every nonempty bounded subset $A$ of $X$ has an infimum $\bigwedge A$ characterized by the metric formula $d(w,\bigwedge A)=\sup_{a\in A}d(w,a)$ for all $w\in X$, and dually a supremum, and that powers and copowers exist. For bounded $X$ this gives an elementary proof, with explicit metric formulas, of the known fact that Isbell-convex Lawvere metric spaces are complete in the sense of enriched category theory; the formulas themselves and the extension to bounded subsets of unbounded $q$-hyperconvex spaces are not covered by the enriched-categorical argument, which requires radii in $[0,\infty]$. Consequently no $T_1$-quasi-metric space with at least two points is $q$-hyperconvex, and the fixed points of every order-preserving self-map of a bounded $q$-hyperconvex space form a nonempty complete lattice. We show that the fixed point set of a nonexpansive self-map need not be a sublattice and that the specialization order need not be distributive. Our main result concerns the continuity of nonexpansive maps. Nonexpansive self-maps of bounded $q$-hyperconvex spaces need not preserve suprema of increasing sequences, and the supremum of the orbit of the least element need not be a fixed point. We prove that for a bounded $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric space the following are equivalent: the space is Smyth complete; every increasing sequence converges to its supremum in the symmetrized metric; every nonexpansive self-map preserves suprema of increasing sequences; every nonexpansive self-map preserves suprema of directed sets; every nonexpansive self-map is Yoneda-continuous. In this case Kleene iteration from the least element converges to the least fixed point; this applies for instance when the symmetrized metric is compact.

papers.title: An approach to topology via lattices of names
papers.abstract: Synthetic topology encompasses various alternatives to the classical definition of a topological space by Hausdorff. In particular, Abstract Stone Duality (ASD) develops the theory of locally compact spaces directly from logic. This study introduces a semi-formal theory of synthetic topology using a first-order version of the intuitionistic modal logic iS4, inspired by a nominalist, dynamic interpretation of the specialization order. The remarkable similarities to ASD include a constructive interpretation of the open-closed duality, overtness of the line, compactness of the unit interval and the nuclei that define closed and open subspaces.
